Highlights:
# Addlink S90 Lite SSD features PCIe Gen 4 NVMe 1.4 Interface and delivers users a significant blazing fast performance boost with sequential read/write speeds of up to 5000/4200MB per second for the latest Intel and AMD platforms' desktops and laptops. The S90 Lite SSD supports HMB technology, which utilizes part of the host memory (DRAM) as if it were its own, and it's built with reliable 3D NAND to offer fantastic value. The S90 Lite is perfect for intensive use for a gamer, content creators, and in-demand engineers with cutting-edge technology.

# Explore the New Era of High Performance

As a PCIe Gen4x4 SSD, the S90 Lite SSD delivers up to ten times faster than a SATA III SSD and around two times faster than Gen3X4 SSD. The S90 Lite SSD is also fully backward compatible with the PCIe Gen3x4 interface.

# SLC Cache & HMB Accelerate the Drive Performance

The drive comes with an SLC caching to deliver better performance for a better user experience. It also supports a host memory buffer (HMB) that allows S90 Lite SSD to proactively pursue higher performance by utilizing the memory resource of the host to maximum random read/write performance for faster loading time & lag-free multitasking.

# Higher Compatibility with Superior Endurance and Reliability

S90 Lite, built with quality 3D NAND Flash, supports the latest LDPC ECC technology, advanced Wear Leveling, Bad Block Management, and Over-Provisioning technology to ensure data accuracy and a longer SSD lifetime. The S90 Lite SSD is ready for the latest Intel and AMD Platforms and compatible with most PCs and laptops from all the major brands. It’s an ideal solution for gaming and hardware enthusiasts who are looking to build or upgrade their PC Furthermore, it is backed by addlink’s limited five years warranty.

## Which NVMe SSD Is Right for You?

Choose Gen3 for everyday upgrades, Gen4 for gaming and content creation, or Gen5 for demanding workloads on compatible PCs. Select a heatsink model where space allows, or use your device’s cooling solution. Match the SSD size to your device: S91 (M.2 2230) for the original ROG Ally; S93 (M.2 2280) matches the ROG Ally X form factor. Check device requirements before installation.

* Performance figures are based on addlink internal testing using specific hardware and configurations. Actual speed may vary by host system, workload, SSD capacity, operating system, and firmware.

##### For Mainstream Upgrades and Value: S90 Lite and S83

##### Not every system needs 7,000+ MB/s speeds. The S90 Lite hits the sweet spot for mainstream users, offering up to 5,000 MB/s read speeds using HMB (Host Memory Buffer) technology to provide fantastic value without sacrificing responsiveness. For budget-conscious builders or those reviving older PCs, the S83 is the perfect entry-level Gen4 drive. At 3,400 MB/s, it is still vastly faster than SATA SSDs and HDDs, providing quick boot times and smooth file handling at an highly affordable price point.

...

##### Q3: What is HMB technology in the S90 Lite?

##### Host Memory Buffer (HMB) technology allows DRAM-less SSDs like the S90 Lite to utilize a small portion of the computer’s system memory (RAM) to cache mapping tables. This significantly improves random read/write performance and responsiveness, allowing the drive to offer excellent performance at a lower cost compared to drives with dedicated onboard DRAM.

##### Para actualizaciones y valor para el usuario promedio: S90 Lite y S83

La S90 Lite es la opción ideal para el usuario promedio, ya que ofrece velocidades de lectura de hasta 5000 MB/s gracias a la tecnología HMB (Host Memory Buffer), proporcionando una excelente relación calidad-precio sin sacrificar la capacidad de respuesta. ##### P3: ¿Qué es la tecnología HMB en la S90 Lite?

##### La tecnología Host Memory Buffer (HMB) permite que las unidades SSD sin DRAM, como la S90 Lite, utilicen una pequeña porción de la memoria del sistema (RAM) del ordenador para almacenar en caché las tablas de asignación. Esto mejora significativamente el rendimiento y la capacidad de respuesta de lectura/escritura aleatoria, lo que permite que la unidad ofrezca un rendimiento excelente a un menor coste en comparación con las unidades con DRAM integrada.
